title: The Top 8 Onboarding Software for Small Businesses in 2026
summary: Streamline new-hire onboarding with top software solutions like Rippling, BambooHR, and Paylocity.
body_markdown:
Most small businesses understand the importance of[onboarding](https://www.rippling.com/glossary/onboarding) , but many lack the dedicated tools and processes needed to deliver a consistent experience as they grow. A delayed payroll setup, or forgotten paperwork can derail a new hire's first week.


Without the right onboarding software, those tasks usually fall to already busy managers or HR teams. Even businesses with an efficient hiring process can lose momentum once a candidate signs the offer letter.


The best onboarding software picks up right where[recruiting](https://www.rippling.com/blog/recruiting-software-for-small-business) leaves off, moving a signed offer letter into tax forms, payroll enrollment, and first-day IT access without anyone re-entering the same information twice. In this guide, we compare eight of the top onboarding software for small businesses in 2026.


## The best onboarding software for small businesses


These eight platforms are ranked on capabilities, pricing transparency, integrations, and G2 and Capterra ratings to find the best onboarding systems.

## 1. Rippling


[Rippling](https://www.rippling.com/rippling-hcm) is designed to bring HR, payroll, IT, and finance into one system, with onboarding as one of its strongest use cases. Instead of managing separate tools, teams can handle offer letters, tax forms, payroll enrollment, and device access from a single dashboard, all built on[Rippling's HRIS](https://www.rippling.com/products/hr/hris-v2) as the underlying system of record.


The onboarding workflow automates much of the setup process, including document collection, approvals, and software or device provisioning, with[Rippling AI](https://www.rippling.com/platform/ai) flagging missing information and routing approvals automatically. Rippling also supports global onboarding, helping companies manage local payroll and compliance requirements without adding another vendor.


Customers highlight this connected approach as a key benefit. Cassandra Margolin, Head of People Operations at Jasper, says Rippling helps "remove that human error" while creating a more personal onboarding experience.


### Pricing


Rippling pricing starts at $8 per employee per month.


### Key features


-


**90-second onboarding:** Businesses can send offer letters, collect tax forms, enroll employees in payroll, and set up their software and device access fast.


-


**Automated compliance tracking:** Rippling makes sure new hires complete I-9s, W-4s, and other mandatory documents, reducing compliance risks.


-


**Seamless IT setup:** The system automatically creates accounts, assigns permissions, and provisions devices, eliminating manual IT work.


-


**Global onboarding capabilities:** Companies can hire and pay employees or contractors worldwide without needing separate payroll or compliance solutions.


-


**Integrated benefits administration:** Employees can enroll in health insurance, retirement plans, and other benefits during the onboarding process without HR manually managing it.


-


**Custom workflows and approvals:** Businesses can tailor onboarding checklists and automate role-specific training, document sign-offs, and account setups, covering the final leg of[full-cycle recruiting](https://www.rippling.com/blog/full-cycle-recruiting) from offer to fully ramped.


-


**30-, 60-, and 90-day check-ins:** HR teams can set up automated reminders for performance reviews, surveys, and training milestones.


-


**Centralized employee data:** Rippling syncs all employee information across HR, payroll, IT, and finance, eliminating duplicate data entry and reducing administrative work.

## **H2: 2. Gusto**


[Gusto](https://www.rippling.com/rippling-vs-gusto) treats onboarding as an extension of payroll rather than a separate system, which makes it a solid, no-frills choice for businesses whose main need is running payroll correctly.


HR teams send offer letters and collect e-signed documents, with direct deposit and tax form collection built directly into the flow. New hires enroll in health insurance and retirement benefits at the same time, and Gusto files new-hire state reporting automatically. Because onboarding is tied so closely to payroll, it works well for companies that don't need heavy customization or IT provisioning.


Workflows are largely preset, which limits how much a company can adapt onboarding to its own process. Gusto’s Employer of Record service also only covers full-time employees in Canada and India, making it less suited for companies planning broader global hiring. Reviewers still rate the interface highly, especially for teams new to HR software.


### Pricing


Gusto's Simple plan starts at $49 per month plus $6 per employee, with Plus and Premium tiers adding multi-state payroll, time tracking, and HR advisory support at higher per-employee rates.


### Key features


-


**Basic digital onboarding:** HR can send offer letters and collect e-signed documents.


-


**Payroll-integrated onboarding:** New hires can input direct deposit details and tax forms within the onboarding flow.


-


**Built-in benefits enrollment:** Employees can sign up for health insurance and retirement plans while completing their onboarding checklist.


-


**New hire state reporting:** Gusto submits necessary paperwork for new employees to the appropriate state agencies.


-


**Limited integrations:** The system connects with some third-party HR tools, but lacks the broad integration capabilities of more advanced onboarding platforms.


-


**Employee self-service portal:** New hires can update their personal information and view payroll details.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Payroll and onboarding setup happen in one flow


Preset workflows leave little room for customization


Beginner-friendly interface for teams new to HR software


EOR support is limited to full-time employees in Canada and India


## 3. BambooHR


[BambooHR](https://www.rippling.com/blog/bamboohr-competitors) is an HR software platform that includes onboarding features, with a focus on basic HR tasks, such as document collection, task tracking, and integrations.


New hires log into a self-service portal to complete forms, upload documents, and review company information, while HR sends offer letters and collects e-signatures. Preboarding tools let businesses start engaging new hires before day one, and preset welcome-email templates and basic task assignments round out the rest.


Reviewers consistently call BambooHR easy to set up, which is a big part of its appeal for smaller teams that don't want a steep learning curve. However, the trade-off is depth. It doesn't automate more complex workflows like IT provisioning or role-based task assignment, so training sessions and team introductions still happen outside the platform.


### Pricing


BambooHR's Core plan starts at around $10 per employee per month, with Pro and Elite tiers priced higher for added performance and compensation tools. Companies with 25 employees or fewer typically pay a flat rate starting around $250 per month regardless of tier.


### Key features


-


**Basic employee self-service onboarding:** New hires can log in to complete forms, upload documents, and access necessary company information.


-


**E-signatures and document storage:** HR can send offer letters and collect e-signed documents.


-


**Preboarding features:** The platform enables businesses to engage new hires before their first day, though with limited customization.


-


**New hire welcome templates:** BambooHR provides preset email templates for welcoming employees.


-


**Limited integration with third-party tools:** The platform connects with some HR and payroll software.


-


**Basic task tracking:** HR can assign tasks to new employees and managers.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Straightforward onboarding process without unnecessary complexity


Lacks full workflow automation for IT provisioning or complex role-based tasks


Supports digital signatures for new hire documents


Response times for support can vary


## **4. Zoho People**


Zoho People's biggest selling point is price. At $1.25 a month per employee, it's hard to find a cheaper way in. It also inherits the deep customizability that defines the rest of the Zoho ecosystem.


It covers the core of employee lifecycle management, including onboarding, attendance, leave tracking, and document storage, all built on customizable forms and approval workflows. Businesses already running other Zoho apps get tight integration across the ecosystem, a real advantage for growing companies that want to shape onboarding around their own process instead of a fixed template.


Reviews are strong on value, but users consistently flag the learning curve. Setting up access controls and complex workflows takes real time upfront, and support can be slow on technical issues. Payroll is also a weak point for companies with requirements outside what Zoho natively supports.


### **Pricing**


Zoho People's Essential HR plan starts at about $1.25 per employee per month, with a limited free tier available for teams of five or fewer. Higher tiers add features like performance management and advanced analytics.


### Key features


-


**Customizable onboarding workflows:** Build forms and approval chains around your own process.


-


**Document tracking:** Collect and store onboarding paperwork digitally.


-


**Employee self-service:** Update information and complete onboarding tasks independently.


-


**Zoho ecosystem integration:** Connect directly with other Zoho apps that a business may already use.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Affordable entry point, especially for small and growing teams


Initial setup and permissions can be confusing


Highly customizable forms and workflows


Payroll features are limited, especially outside the US


## 5. Paycor


[Paycor](https://www.rippling.com/paycor-competitors) pairs payroll with onboarding tools built around document management, compliance tracking, and task assignment, aimed squarely at small and mid-sized teams.


HR builds automated checklists with deadlines it can track directly, while new hires e-sign tax documents and policies on their own schedule. Preboarding support means welcome emails and required materials can go out before a start date, and the self-service portal handles much of onboarding without constant HR involvement.


Some reviewers report the app crashing mid-task, and contract setup is less intuitive than expected; workflows are also less flexible than some competitors offer. What consistently wins people over is task assignment: reviewers point to role-specific work and progress tracking as a genuine time-saver.


### Pricing


Pricing is custom and quote-based across four tiers, with reported starting costs around $99 per month plus a per-employee fee for its entry-level plan.


### Key features


-


**Digital document collection:** E-sign tax documents and company policies.


-


**Automated onboarding checklists:** Assign tasks, set deadlines, and track progress.


-


**Preboarding capabilities:** Send welcome emails and paperwork before day one.


-


**Self-service portal:** Complete tasks and update information independently.


-


**Basic compliance tracking:** Track required onboarding steps to help ensure completion.

## 6. Deel


Hiring internationally often creates a maze of compliance requirements, worker classifications, and payment processes to manage across different countries.[Deel](https://www.rippling.com/rippling-vs-deel) helps simplify that complexity by combining global payroll and compliance support with onboarding tools for businesses hiring international employees and contractors.


The platform helps employers generate legally compliant contracts, collect tax forms and IDs, and track compliance requirements across markets. New hires can also complete much of the onboarding process themselves through a self-service portal, where they upload documents and review contracts.


Deel earns strong reviews for helping businesses manage international hiring and pay employees and contractors in multiple currencies without relying on a separate payroll provider. However, the platform focuses more on compliance and payments than the broader employee onboarding experience, which may limit teams looking for features like structured training plans or IT provisioning.


### Pricing


Deel's contractor management starts at about $49 per contractor per month, while its Employer of Record service starts at roughly $599 per employee per month, with global payroll priced separately for companies with existing entities.


### Key features

**Contract generation:** Create legally compliant contracts for different worker classifications.


-


**Document management:** Collect and store tax forms, IDs, and other onboarding documents.


-


**Automated compliance tracking:** Monitor adherence to international labor regulations.


-


**Payment processing:** Pay employees and contractors across countries from one system.


-


**Customizable onboarding workflows:** Configure preboarding, contract sign-offs, and compliance steps.

## **What is onboarding software for small businesses?**


Onboarding software (also called an onboarding system or new hire onboarding software) replaces manual busywork with a structured digital process.


Most platforms combine e-signatures, task tracking, and automated reminders, and many integrate directly with payroll and benefits, so a new hire’s information only has to be entered once. Onboarding software is one of the more common entry points into small business automation because onboarding is often the first process a growing company decides to stop managing manually.


The term “onboarding software” gets used loosely elsewhere. Some products marketed as customer onboarding solutions serve a completely different purpose, helping companies onboard clients rather than employees. This guide focuses on[HR technology](https://www.rippling.com/blog/hr-technology) built specifically to manage new hires, not customer relationships.


## Why do small businesses need onboarding software tools?


Bringing on a new hire goes beyond just filling a vacant position. It involves setting the new hire up for success from the get-go. Small businesses generally work with limited time and resources, and a disorganized onboarding process only makes things harder. Without the right system in place, mistakes pile up, HR wastes time, and new hires struggle to get up to speed.


Here’s why small businesses need onboarding software to keep things running smoothly:


### Every hire counts


On a five- or ten-person team, one disorganized start can throw off a whole quarter. It's one of the[top HR challenges](https://www.rippling.com/blog/10-hr-challenges-in-2026) small businesses are already facing in 2026, and one that's easy to underestimate until it costs real time. A stalled process delays the work a new hire was brought on to do, and it's usually an owner or HR lead who ends up absorbing the fallout.


### First impressions matter


Employee onboarding involves more than paperwork. It’s the first real experience someone has with a company. A strong onboarding process sets the tone for new employees and helps them feel welcome. When businesses get onboarding right, employees are likely to feel more confident, engaged, and ready to stay long term.


### Mistakes cost time and money


Small teams can’t afford onboarding mistakes. Not getting a payroll setup right, skipping compliance steps, or delaying employee training can create frustration for both HR and new hires. Then there's the fixing of these issues, which wastes time and can slow down operations. A structured onboarding process prevents these problems before they happen.


### Employees expect a good experience


Feeling valued shapes how a new hire sees the company long after their Feeling valued shapes how a new hire sees the company long after their first week is over. Good software for onboarding new employees helps create a consistent welcome experience, rather than leaving it up to whoever remembers to make introductions and check in.


## 5 reasons small businesses need onboarding software


By replacing manual processes with automation, onboarding software can help companies save time, reduce errors, and give their new hires a smoother start. Below are some of the major benefits of using onboarding software in a small business.


### 1. Efficiency


Manual onboarding eats up valuable time. HR teams juggle emails, forms, and reminders, which often leads to confusion and delays. Manually following an onboarding checklist makes it easy to miss steps and slows everything down.


An onboarding platform fixes this by centralizing tasks, automating paperwork, and keeping everything in one place. Instead of chasing signatures or tracking tasks manually, businesses can let the software handle it. What might take hours without onboarding software can take just minutes with it.


***Example:*** *A small marketing agency hires a new graphic designer. Without onboarding software, HR spends hours emailing forms, collecting signatures, and setting up software accounts one by one. With an onboarding platform, the designer receives a single link that walks them through signing documents, setting up their email, and accessing design tools. And it does it all in under 30 minutes.*


### 2. Compliance


Small businesses can’t afford compliance mistakes. Missing key documents, skipping legal requirements, or mishandling tax forms can lead to penalties. Onboarding software can help keep everything in check by automating compliance steps, ensuring the right forms get signed, and securely storing records for audits.


***Example:*** *A local café hires a new barista. The café needs to collect an I-9 form for work eligibility and tax withholding documents for payroll from the new barista. Without an onboarding system, the manager collects these by hand and may forget key forms. With onboarding software, the barista receives automatic prompts to upload their documents before their first shift, helping the café comply with labor laws.*


### 3. Better employee experience


A clunky onboarding process can make new hires feel lost before they even get started. An onboarding platform can do a good job of simplifying the experience. It can make it easy for them to access documents, complete training, and get introduced to the team. A smooth start can help new hires feel confident, engaged, and connected with the company culture from their very first day.


***Example:*** *A tech startup hires a remote developer. Without onboarding software, the developer has to email HR for information and wait days to get access to necessary tools. With an onboarding platform, they log in on day one, complete their paperwork online, watch a welcome video from leadership, and instantly access Slack and Jira. This helps them feel like part of the team right away.*


### 4. Automate HR processes


Without automation, HR teams may spend hours on repetitive tasks. For instance, sending welcome emails, collecting forms, and setting up accounts. Onboarding software takes care of these steps automatically. This can free up HR to focus on bigger priorities like employee engagement and business growth.


***Example:*** *A boutique law firm hires a legal assistant. Without an onboarding platform, HR manually sends IT setup instructions, tracks down signed NDAs, and adds the assistant to the payroll system. With automation, the assistant follows step-by-step instructions, signs all necessary documents electronically, and completes payroll enrollment, all without HR lifting a finger.*


### 5. Streamline new employee training


Onboarding doesn’t stop at the initial paperwork. New hires often need training to do their jobs well. With the right onboarding platform, businesses can seamlessly schedule training sessions, track progress, and make sure employees get the information they need to succeed. Instead of relying on scattered emails and informal check-ins, companies can deliver a structured training experience that sets employees up for success from the start.


***Example:*** *A family-owned construction company hires a site supervisor. The role requires OSHA safety training, but without onboarding software, training happens through printed manuals and in-person meetings, leading to inconsistent learning. With an onboarding platform, the supervisor watches interactive safety modules, completes quizzes, and receives certification before stepping on site.*


Automate onboarding — from offer letters to device shipping — so new employees hit the ground running.

## How to choose the best small business onboarding software


The wrong onboarding platform can create more problems than it solves. Here’s how to pick the best onboarding software for your company:


### Step 1. Evaluate your business needs and goals


Start with the basics. What’s slowing down your onboarding process right now? Are new hires getting lost in paperwork? Is HR spending too much time on manual tasks? Do employees struggle with training because there’s no structured system?


Make a list of the biggest pain points. If compliance is an issue, you’ll probably need a platform that automates document collection and tracks deadlines. If remote hiring is part of your business, look for software with digital signatures and virtual training tools. The goal is to find an onboarding system that fixes your specific problems, not just one with fancy features you won’t use.


### Step 2. Consider your present (and future) budget


Price matters, but so does value. Some onboarding platforms charge per employee, while others have a flat monthly fee. Some include payroll and benefits, while others charge extra for those features.


Think about what you can afford now, but also plan for the future. If your business is growing, you don’t want to switch software in a year because your current plan becomes too expensive. Compare different pricing models and check if the platform offers a scalable option. It's important that it grows with you.


### Step 3. Compare software integrations with current tools


Your onboarding system should work with the tools you already use. If your payroll software,[HR platform](https://www.rippling.com/blog/hrms-small-business) , or applicant tracking system (ATS) doesn’t sync with the new software, onboarding could remain a manual nightmare.


Make a list of must-have integrations. If you already have a payroll system in place, ensure the onboarding platform connects seamlessly. If your team relies on a specific communication tool, check if the system can add new hires to the right channels straight away. The fewer manual steps, the better.


### Step 4. Check user reviews and customer support quality


A platform can look great on paper but be a headache in real life. Read real user reviews, especially from businesses of your size, to see if it actually delivers on its promises. Look for feedback on things like ease of use, setup time, and customer support responsiveness.


Some platforms offer 24/7 chat, while others take days to reply. Try asking a pre-sales question and see how fast they respond. If getting help is already a hassle before you sign up, it probably won’t get any better later.


## 7 features to look for in onboarding systems


Not every feature matters equally. These seven make the biggest difference for a small team.


### 1. Electronic documents and forms management


New hires can complete required paperwork online, reducing the manual follow-up that often causes delays and misplaced documents.


### 2. Compliance


Missing a single required document, like an I-9 or a state-specific form, can mean real fines. A platform that tracks deadlines and flags gaps automatically closes that risk before it becomes a problem.


### 3. Integration options


Onboarding platforms use integrations to keep employee data connected across systems. Without them, teams may need to enter the same information into separate tools for payroll, HR, and applicant tracking, which takes time and increases the risk of errors.


### 4. Customizability


A one-size-fits-all approach doesn’t work. The onboarding experience should reflect company policies, branding, and industry requirements. Without customization, businesses risk delivering a generic process that leaves new hires feeling disconnected or unprepared for their specific roles.


### 5. Scalability


What works with five employees rarely holds up with 50. Switching systems mid-growth is expensive and disruptive, so it's worth choosing a platform that can grow alongside your plans to[scale the business](https://www.rippling.com/blog/how-to-scale-business) , rather than one you'll have to replace the moment headcount jumps.


### 6. User-friendliness


If HR and new hires struggle to use the software, it defeats the purpose. Complicated software leads to frustration, delays, and incomplete onboarding steps. Employees should be able to navigate the system without constant IT support.


### 7. Mobile access


A strong onboarding platform should work on mobile devices, so employees can complete tasks from anywhere. Remote workers, field employees, and retail staff often don’t have access to a computer on their first day. Mobile access can make onboarding flexible and convenient.

## Frequently asked questions


How long does onboarding take?


Anywhere from a few days to several weeks, depending on how structured the process is. Without a system, HR ends up chasing documents and answering the same questions repeatedly. Platforms like Rippling can complete the setup itself in about 90 seconds, though training and ramp-up still take longer.


How do you onboard remote employees?


Using the same checklist that works in person, just delivered digitally: contracts, equipment, logins, virtual introductions, and training, all handled without a shared office. The best platforms automate each step, so a remote hire has what they need on day one without HR tracking it by hand.


How much does onboarding software cost?


It depends on the platform and how many employees you have. Some platforms charge a flat fee, others charge per employee, and advanced features like payroll or IT provisioning cost more. Weigh that against what a disorganized process already costs you, in terms of HR hours and mistakes that take even longer to fix.


What are 4 C's for onboarding?


The 4 C’s of onboarding are:


-


**Compliance:** Making sure new hires complete necessary paperwork, tax forms, and legal documents.


-


**Clarification:** Ensuring employees understand their role, responsibilities, and expectations.


-


**Culture:** Introducing employees to company culture, including values, mission, and workplace dynamics.


-


**Connection:** Helping employees build relationships with their team, managers, and company leadership.


A strong employee onboarding process incorporates all four to set new hires up for long-term success.


What is the best employee management software for small business?


The best employee management software depends on what a business needs. A strong system should handle applicant tracking, payroll, time tracking, hr analytics, performance management, and onboarding process automation.


Rippling is a strong option for small businesses that want to manage HR, IT, payroll, and spend workflows in one platform. Its unified approach can help teams manage more of the employee lifecycle from a single system, though businesses with more specialized needs may prefer providers that focus on specific areas.


Can onboarding be automated?


Yes—[onboarding automation](https://www.rippling.com/blog/automated-onboarding-workflows) is a common feature across most top people management platforms for small businesses. Each platform offers its own capabilities, but with Rippling, you can automate admin work across your HR, IT, and finance departments as your new hires start.
